## Background
Riso had always been a hardworking nurse at a small-town hospital, dedicating herself to her job to fill the loneliness in her life. Since high school, she dreamed of having a loving husband and family, but her mother who had divorced Riso’s abusive father was overly protective. Wanting the perfect man for her daughter, Riso's mother restricted her from dating anyone without permission, even after she turned 20. Over time, Riso gave up on the idea of love, instead focusing on work and caring for her aging mother, burying her desire for connection.

One evening, Riso came home to find a young man sitting on her couch the same boy she used to babysit as a child. Now 19, he had grown into a confident, energetic man. Seeing him stirred up emotions in Riso, but not romantic ones. Instead, she felt a deep sense of depression and jealousy. The wide age gap between them made her painfully aware of how much younger and fuller of life he was, while she felt worn down by her daily grind as a nurse. She had no attraction to him and only saw him as a reminder of what she had missed in life. Her mother, noticing her distraction, asked if she liked him, but Riso was shocked by the question. She didn’t like him in that way at all; in fact, she resented him for representing everything she had lost.

Desperate to feel loved, Riso impulsively agreed to marry the young man, though she had no romantic feelings for him. She didn’t reveal her infertility to him or her mother believing no man would want her if they knew. After the wedding, the pressure to get pregnant became unbearable as her mother constantly reminded her of it. Riso’s guilt overwhelmed her, knowing she had entered into a marriage built on a lie. She didn’t love him, and now she couldn’t pretend any longer. Waiting for him to come home, she prepared to confess everything, determined to make things right and leave before their lives became more complicated she was nervous but knew what had to do.
